notes.title: Uncrewed 2 Announcement
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=NuowUfjYs3M;full][/previewyoutube]

It has come time to announce that [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3657500/Uncrewed_2/]Uncrewed 2[/url], a sequel and a successor to Uncrewed, is currently active development! 

While a direct sequel to the original game, Uncrewed 2 takes a different approach to many gameplay aspects of the game and tries to marry the formula of classic RTS with unit design abilities more closely.

[h3]Base Building[/h3]

Uncrewed 2 features a more traditional approach to base building - the player is free to build anywhere on the map with only the help of a builder unit, eliminating the requirement of special build pads. The variety of structure types has also been expanded, including the addition of effective defensive structures.

[h3]Maps[/h3]

Map design is also very different in Uncrewed 2. Due to more emphasis on base building in the game, the maps feature more open areas, they are easier to navigate and have distinct levels of elevation to accommodate the new vision system. 

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]

The gameplay has been greatly streamlined and brought in line with the feel of more traditional RTS. For example, the reliance on weapon ammunition and energy for movement has been done away with. The vision system has also been greatly expanded upon with small ground units unable to see up large cliffs.

[h3]Unit Designer[/h3]

The unit designer has seen many significant changes, with the most the prominent being the block sculpting system. It is now much more robust and completely integrated into the unit designer itself. You can change the shapes of multiple blocks at once without the need of a separate screen or long lists of custom modules.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25738567/02d15c38d39d708f9e360f52e42f966194e2b7c5.png[/img]

[h3]Weapon Crafting[/h3]

One of the key new additions in Uncrewed 2 is the weapon crafting system. Unlike in the original, where the player has a selection of non-customizable weapons, all the weapons in Uncrewed 2 can be crafted using a weapon designer.  

You can now mix and match ammo types, firing mechanisms and barrel lengths, all of which affects important weapon characteristics - firing ranges, firing rates, damage output, status effects, etc.

[h3]Development and Feedback[/h3]

Thank you everyone for supporting the original Uncrewed! If you are interested you can wishlist [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3657500/Uncrewed_2/]Uncrewed 2[/url]. It is slated for release sometime in 2026. It is expected to come out as a full release without an early access phase.

If you have any questions or general feedback you are also welcome to comment below or head to  [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/3657500/discussions/]Uncrewed 2 discussion forums[/url]

notes.title: Moving to 64-bit, Improved Performance and Rapid Fire Mode
notes.notes:
[h1]64-bit, Improved Performance and legacy OS support[/h1]

When Uncrewed first started development, 32-bit hardware was still ubiquitous and 32-bit OS versions had a significant market share. Today, as far as gaming is concerned, virtually all platforms out there are 64-bit. Up to this point Uncrewed was an exclusively 32-bit application, which caused degraded performance and even stability issues in some cases. 

As of this update Uncrewed has been ported to 64-bit and will no longer support 32-bit versions of Windows. The move to a 64-bit build brings improved performance (up to 20% in some cases) and eliminates all possible stability issues when playing on maximum settings with large number of units, as well as greatly improves expandability and modding potential.

Because of this change Uncrewed will no longer run on any Windows XP version, and as of this update only the 64-bit versions of Windows 7, 8/8.1, 10 and 11 are officially supported. Running the game via Proton will also require a 64-bit Linux.

[h1]Rapid Fire Mode[/h1]

This update also introduces the concept of rules to custom games. You can now play all available maps (including your own and those from the workshop) with non-standard sets of rules provided the maps don't use custom scripts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25738567/be09d5583d59c867bb862cfc9968bcda606edc7c.png[/img]

[list]
[*] [i]Rapid Fire[/i] rules increase all weapon ammo capacity by 10x. It is now the default rule-set for custom games. This change reduces unit micro-management which in turn makes the games feel much faster and action oriented. Try it out for yourself!
[*] [i]Classic[/i] rules are how the game used to play before this update. Some players may still find this mode to be a better experience, but it is overall harder and slower.
[/list]
[h1]Other[/h1]

[list]
[*] Balance changes: 

[olist]
[*] Resource amount per pile has been quadrupled (going up from 1000 pellets per pile to 4000 pellets per pile);
[*] [i]Rotary Gun[/i] damage increased from 1 to 1.5 (DPS increase from 4.0 to 6.0);
[*] [i]Revolver Cannon[/i] damage increased from 2.0 to 2.5, firing rate increased from 1.5 to 2.0 (DPS increase from 3.0 to 5.0);
[*] [i]IR Launcher[/i] firing rate increased from 0.7 to 0.8 (DPS increase from 14.0 to 16.0);[/olist]
[*] Fixed an issue where the mouse cursor wouldn't stay inside the game window after Alt-Tabbing once on multi-monitor setups.
[*] Fixed UI issues that made some buttons unreachable on the lowest supported resolution (1366x768).
[/list]
For the full list of changes see the patch notes.

notes.title: Out Of Early Access, More Updates To Come
notes.notes:
[h1]Out of Early Access![/h1]

Over three years of development after the initial release, the Early Access tag no longer accurately represents the game state. So today Uncrewed has its official full release!

The game features a complete stand-alone campaign, decently large selection of modules of all types to build units with. There is also the ability to create your own modules and maps, Steam Workshop support and more! The game still has room for growth, however its current state does not warrant an Early Access tag. 

[h1]Upcoming Campaign Expansion[/h1]

The work on the campaign expansion continues, and it is planned for release later this year. The game already features a stand-alone campaign, but because of a considerable popular demand it was decided to develop an expansion for the game. Like other all updates before the campaign expansion will be added to the base game with no extra purchases required.

[h1]Other Content Updates[/h1]

Although the Early Access phase of the development has ended, the game will still receive content updates. In short term there are plans to add more features to the map making tools. The addition of new modules is also very likely. So stay tuned, and your feedback is always welcome!

[h1]Patches[/h1]

Like before, the game will receive patches for balance changes, bug fixes and other minor improvements.

[i]Patch Notes:[/i]
[list]
[*]Changed aiming behaviour for smaller weapons. Weapons now lock on to targets faster and are able to fire at fast moving flying units;
[*]Scripting improvements and bug fixes;
[*]Minor interface improvements and fixes.
[/list]

notes.title: Update: Portable Reactor
notes.notes:
[h1]What's new?[/h1]

This update introduces the Portable Reactor module, and a few other changes and improvements to the game.

[h1]Portable Reactor[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25738567/e6d80f9db78aed0f6cde5b47cf0304d9825dada3.png[/img]

The [i]Portable Reactor[/i] module generates energy and recharges the batteries. Although they are heavy and expensive, any number of portable reactors can be installed on a unit. The Portable Reactor also requires an Energy Lab.

[h1]Launch Command[/h1]

As of this update, units equipped with Grenade Launchers or Artillery Guns can fire at any point on the map by using the [i]Launch[/i] command. Firing at a fixed spot can be a way to deny that area to your opponent, and a way to hit fast moving units with slow projectiles if unit movement can be predicted.

[h1]Other[/h1]
[list]
[*]Keyboard scrolling is now re-mappable (Arrow Keys by default);
[*]Battery storage capacity is now displayed in the module gallery;
[*]Unit sound responses are now not activated on every action;
[*]Minor bug fixes and improvements.
[/list]

notes.title: Update: New Game Plus
notes.notes:
[h1]What's new?[/h1]
This update introduces the new game plus mode for the main campaign.

[h1]New Game Plus[/h1]
As of this update, after completing the campaign on any difficulty a new mode for the campaign is unlocked. The [i]New Game Plus[/i] can be accessed when starting a new campaign by chosing "New Game Plus" as the difficulty level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25738567/33d174d03f9c6720f9adec7ea3e4fb33c1b6c19e.png[/img]

Some of the key differences between [i]New Game Plus[/i] and other difficulty levels are:
[list]
[*]AI opponents play to the best of their abilities and choose the best units available to them;
[*]There are no restrictions on technologies from the very start of the campaign;
[*]The maximum number of unit slots is available on every map;
[*]Research Data locations are randomized.
[/list]

New Game Plus difficulty is the hardest difficulty currently available for the campaign. There's now an additional achievement for completing the campaign on this difficulty.

[h1]Other[/h1]
Other changes included with this update:
[list]
[*]Balance changes: enemy units can no longer be lifted up with skymagnets unless under influence of an EMP.
[*]Minor bug fixes and improvements.
[/list]

notes.title: Upcoming Updates
notes.notes:
[h1]Long-term Content Plans[/h1]

Currently the game features a complete stand-alone campaign, and a decently large selection of modules of all types. There is also the ability to create your own modules and maps. In many ways the game has outgrown its initial scope. Of course there is always room for improvement.

Over the course of development, the community has expressed interest in more single-player content. Taking this and other factors into consideration, the next major content update will feature a campaign expansion. Additionally, any new modules that may be added, will also likely to arrive with that update.

As of right now, there is no set release date for the update, but it will be provided further down the development cycle!

[h1]Other Updates[/h1]

There are other areas of the game that will be getting updates in the meantime. That includes balance updates, updates to the multiplayer component of the game, and the map editor.

As always, your feedback is appreciated, and stay tuned for more news about the game!

notes.title: Update: Map Editor is out!
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/0243492a867529a4f1a6298b8f303930deb6ac93.png[/img]

[h1]What's new?[/h1]

This update brings the ability to create, edit and share custom maps. This is the first update in the series of updates aimed to give the community flexible tools for map and game mode creation.

[h1]Map Composer[/h1]

The toolset which provides map making facilities is called the [b]Map Composer[/b]. To access it, click the [i]Map Composer[/i] button in the main menu. 

To create a new map click the [i]New Map...[/i] button - this action will immediately launch the map editor. You are also be able to manage and share your maps from this menu.

The map editor itself gives you the ability to customize every aspect of the map. As mentioned before, more tools will be added to the map editor to enable further customization, as well as ease the process of map making.

[h1]Documentation[/h1]

Currently there's not much in the way of documentation available for the editor, nor the scripting language. This will be rectified in the upcoming days - help, tutorials, and references are coming, so stay tuned!

[h1]Other[/h1]

The update also brings slight improvements and changes to the interface, as well as various bug fixes. Among more notable changes - the removal of the [i]Skirmish[/i] button; it has been replaced with the [i]Custom Game[/i] button. No functionality has been lost - this is just a menu change to better fit the new features.

Your feedback regarding the map editing tools or any other topic is, as always, appreciated.

Update: Infrared Homing Missiles, Large Jet Engines
notes.notes:
[h1]What's new?[/h1]

This update adds a new missile launcher, a new jet engine, introduces expanded post-match statistics, brings several balance changes, and other fixes and improvements.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/f19aff33c97ea04894fac8a06cefae0ac1f0c2b1.png[/img]

[h1]Infrared Homing Missile Launcher[/h1]

It has been noted that land armies can be quickly overwhelmed by very mobile flying units, making non-flying units redundant in many scenarios. In order to mitigate this issue, as of this update the game now features a new powerful anti-air weapon called [b]Infrared Homing Missile Launcher[/b]. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/492e9f9e61c0aab132c747d990e7fb1604746cff.png[/img]

The weapon carries several large missiles capable of tracking and following enemy units with thermal singatures (e.g. active jet engines). Once launched at a hot target, the missile is almost certain to hit it - having a [i]Laser[/i] equipped is about the only way to stop the projectile. The weapon also works against all other targets, albeit without homing capabilities.

Here is a short video demonstrating how it performs:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2rkqWRK5kLs
[h1]Large Jet Engines[/h1]

In previous versions of the game, flying units above 1000 kg could incorrectly fly with too few jet engines. This update alters this behavior such that very heavy flying units (above 1000 kg) will require much more thrust from jet engines to operate. 

Due to the fact that equipping a unit with a large number of small jet engines might be difficult and impractical, the game now has a new jet engine - the [b]Large 5-Nozzle Rocket Jet Engine[/b]. It behaves exactly the same as its smaller counterpart, except for the doubled thrust and increased cost, and size. It should aid in the design of larger fliers.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/9dc23f63a124ca42737e346eb31ebaa99766106b.png[/img]

[h1]Post-Match Statistics[/h1]

As of this update, the post-match screen has been significantly reworked for both single-player and multi-player modes. It now most notably includes detailed per-unit statistics. This feature could be useful for unit design performance analysis. There are plans to expand game statistics even further in future updates.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/d8d646a684b8f09896ffb1130a158def4ca1628d.png[/img]

[h1]Other[/h1]
[list]
[*]Balance changes:
[list]
[*][i]Cannon[/i] DPS increased to 7.0, and its vertical aiming limitation has been lifted;
[*][i]Large Revolver Cannon[/i] DPS increased to 10.0;
[/list]
[*]Particle performance improvements;
[*]Minor interface fixes and improvements.
[/list]

Update: Introducing the new Custom Module Designer
notes.notes:
[h1]What's new?[/h1]

This update brings a new custom module editor, which adds a new degree of flexibility to module modification systems in the game.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/2fb1cc4c1c7da1b074750616e2d1e91d41135ea4.png[/img]

[h1]Custom Module Designer[/h1]

As of this update, in addition to the already existing custom module designer, there is now a new custom module designer available. It can be accessed via the module gallery by selecting the special Create Custom Module item.

Instead of relying on a chain of simple deformation modifiers, the new designer allows direct manipulation of the geometry by the way of a control box. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/36e954f1010b1b58ddf5de6357f91c9ef673bb6e.png[/img]

The control box has eight movable vertices, and twelve deformable edges - it envelopes the module, and all changes made to its element positions are reflected in the geometry. This system gives a much finer control over the look of the module, especially when in comes to organic-looking curves and shapes.

The new editor also adds the ability to modify module face styles. Every custom module has six faces, each of which can have one of the three face styles (connector, recessed, or protruding). This feature can be useful for removing unwanted connectors. It is also possible to change the module material at any point during the design process.

The new designer does not replace the existing modifier-based module designer, which serves a slightly different purpose (modification of existing standard modules).

[h1]Other[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue where scaled decals would sometimes fail to apply on flat surfaces; 
[*]Fixed an issue where viewing units in the unit viewer would sometimes cause a crash;
[*]Fixed campaign script issues that would sometimes appear after loading a saved game;
[*]Minor bug fixes and interface improvements.
[/list]

notes.title: Update: New Wheels, Large Revolver Cannon, EMP Resistance
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/0333c956d9878bf38e73181cea810a5651798bb3.png[/img]

[h1]What's new?[/h1]

This update introduces three new wheel modules, a new large weapon, EMP resistance rating, and several other changes and improvements to the game.

[h1]New Wheels[/h1]

Among the newly introduced wheels are - a new Motorized Wheel, a new Large Motorized Wheel, and a Very Large Wheel. The first two are variations of existing wheel modules, featuring a less enclosed design. The [b]Very Large Wheel[/b] is a completely new propulsion module that has much better all-terrain characteristics. Naturally it also features a more powerful motor. Note that because of its large size, the stability control system will throttle back the wheel significantly, if used on smaller vehicles. If you are confident in your vehicle design, it might be a good idea to reduce the Stability Control influence or disable it altogether.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/e26f8569ce81179899e28ab6aad1212df6d36bc5.png[/img]

[h1]Large Revolver Cannon[/h1]

[b]Large Revolver Cannon[/b] is a companion weapon to the recently added Large Rotary Gun. Though not as powerful as the large rotary gun DPS-wise, Large Revolver Cannon has a higher hit damage, and a longer range. Just like the rotary gun, it is invulnerable to EMPs, and can discharge up close without damaging the firing unit.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/b3ce7e5a8aec71e9a51a90e4abf39050f80312cc.png[/img]

[h1]EMP Resistance Rating[/h1]

As of this update, every unit has an EMP resistance rating associated with it. The higher the rating, the lower the stun time, and the energy drain from a single EMP hit (up to a point). Unit's EMP rating, and its effect are displayed when hovering over HP readout in the unit designer.

EMP resistance rating can be increased by installing EMP resistive structural modules. Module EMP resistance is displayed in the module gallery. Not all structural modules have EMP rating increase associated with them, and usually the heavier modules will feature this armor bonus.

Please note that non-resistive modules do not decrease the unit's overall EMP rating, so it's not necessary to use just the EMP resistive modules to achieve good anti-EMP performance. 

[h1]Centered UI[/h1]

The main command bar is now centered by default. It can be stretched across the whole screen (as it was before this change) by pressing Ctrl+Page Up, or via the Options menu. It can be then switched back to the centered position by pressing Ctrl+Page Down. This change was brought about by the fact that the stretched bar is very wasteful on larger, wide-screen, and ultra-wide screen displays. 

[h1]Other[/h1]
[list]
[*]Very large, and wide walkers no longer get stuck when moving along the factory conveyor;
[*]Decal designer: back-facing decals no longer interfere with front-facing decal selection;
[*]Reverse steering improvements;
[*]Units will no longer try to unnecessarily move away from each other when parked in close proximity;
[*]Minor interface improvements;
[*]A few synchronization issues solved when playing multiplayer games under high latency network conditions;
[*]Balance changes: Revolver Gun - DPS increased to 3.0 (from 2.6), ammo capacity increased to 120.
[*]Large Rotary Gun cost increased; both Large Rotary Gun and Large Revolver Cannon require an explosives lab and a propulsion lab;
[*]AI: Bots will now take EMP resistance into account;
[*]Other minor bug fixes and improvements.
[/list]

notes.title: Update: New Sandbox Features, Large Rotary Gun
notes.notes:
[h1]What's new?[/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/dd4537dff1378afb5f9bfa0e35f8bce3179b386f.png[/img]

[h1]Sandbox[/h1]

As of this update it is now possible in Sandbox mode to turn your own units into enemy units. To achieve this use the [b]Switch Teams[/b] command, which appears alongside all other issuable unit commands.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/a6abeb9db3e0336941d6695b2743d820cf2d2667.png[/img]

notes.title: Update Notes: Unit Anchoring
notes.notes:
[h1]What's new?[/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/f97fceb776bf7a4936c07a5c51ff467bff449b56.png[/img]

This update introduces the ability to anchor units to the ground, essentially turning these units into custom static structures. The update also brings several general improvements and changes.

[h1]Anchoring[/h1]

To anchor a unit to the ground, first a [b]Mount[/b] needs to be constructed on any standard-sized build pad, and then the unit can be either dropped, or moved there. Provided the unit is equipped with an [b]Anchor[/b] module, it will automatically attach itself to the mount. From there the unit can be detached, or rotated in-place (90 degree increments).

As mentioned in the previous announcement, when anchored, units become completely immovable, and thus will no longer experience recoil, or be susceptible to ramming. Anchored units are automatically repaired, recharged, and restocked via their mounts; though the repair speed is slower than that of dedicated repair facilities.

Other changes and improvements introduced with this update include:
[list]
[*]Units will now try to use not just the closest, but the best repair facility available. For example, units will generally prefer repair pads that are surrounded by repair bays. 
[*]Fixed an issue where Skymagnet equipped fliers were unable to transport some very large units.
[*]Fixed an issue where some hotkeys would conflict with text input boxes in the unit designer.
[*]Fixed an issue where healers set to auto-heal would automatically charge their targets up to 50%. Now automatic charging will occur when the charge falls below 50%, and will continue until either the unit is fully charged, or other more critical target becomes available.
[*]Balance changes: Plasma Thrower now deals more damage (18.0 DPS), its targeting speed has been increased, and the cost has been reduced (80 Pellets, 45 Heavy Pellets).
[*]General minor bug-fixes and improvements.
[/list]

notes.title: Update: Enhanced Unit Autonomous Behavior, Better Core Utilization
notes.notes:
[h1]What's new?[/h1]

This update introduces a new unit behavior mode that lets the units automatically recharge, restock, and repair themselves, freeing up the player to focus on more strategic tasks. 
The update also improves CPU core utilization, which leads to significant performance gains in many scenarios. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/cc0d561fcd3e05f75bc894e237e1632dc7e42bdc.jpg[/img]

[h1]Autonomous Behavior[/h1]

[b]Auto Maintenance[/b] - units that have this behavior enabled, will automatically try to recharge, restock ammo, and repair themselves. For example, harvesters will seek out the nearest repair pad when their energy dips below a certain level; they will resume mining as soon as charging is completed. This behavior is enabled by default for all units, but it can be toggled on and off.

Additional information:
[list]
[*]Units generally will try to perform maintenance only when idle, or when it is absolutely required to perform their tasks;
[*]Units set to [i]Hold[/i] position will not perform automatic maintenance;
[*]Units will not try to repair themselves unless they are also set to [i]Defend[/i] position;
[*]Units will not recharge or restock their ammo if the repair facility is too far away unless it is required to perform their tasks; flying units are the exception - they will always try to recharge themselves when needed.
[/list]

[h1]Better Performance[/h1]

With better CPU core utilization the game performance has been significantly improved in many scenarios - especially when it comes to large scale battles, and multi-player games with lots of units on the field. 

Note: For maximum performance gains, the CPU needs to have at least 3 cores (4 cores are recommended); dual-core setups should also experience performance improvements.

[h1]Other[/h1]
[list]
[*]Multi-player performance improvements
[*]Various interface fixes and improvements.
[/list]

notes.title: Update Notes: Expanded Naval Base Building, Submarines, EMPs and Railguns
notes.notes:
[h1]What's new?[/h1]

The update features expanded naval base building, a new propulsion module ([b]Ballast Tank[/b]) that allows for creation of submarines, two new weapons, a new naval-oriented skirmish map called [b]Islands[/b], as well as many other less major improvements and additions.

The previously announced advanced AI difficulty customization still requires some work, and will come out on May 4th. Sorry for the delay.

[h1]Submarines[/h1]

Submarines can be built with the help of a new propulsion module called Ballast Tank. Equipped with enough of these modules, a unit can freely submerge and surface at any time when in water.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/0ece28736fe33eed4253f01666ea22d154ab3969.png[/img]

When submerged, submarines are less vulnerable to some types of damage (kinetic weapons do less damage, lasers and EMPs have no effect at all). These units can be very advantageous on maps with large bodies of water.

[h1]Marine Factories[/h1]

[b]Marine Factories[/b] are factories that can be built on build pads which are placed in water. They act the same as field factories with the exception that they can be used to deploy units that cannot move on land.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/427993cec32b36901613fe20b58b9e9b2a2d6df2.png[/img]

In addition to the factories, almost all other buildings can be built on water. The exceptions are - [b]Repair Pads[/b] and [b]Resource Chutes[/b]. In order to repair units directly on water, a new building has been introduced - the [b]Repair Bay[/b]. It can be built on water, and will repair, recharge and restock all units that surround it (one by one). If placed close enough, multiple repair bays can target a single unit, which will increase the repair speed. 

[h1]Large Railgun and EMP[/h1]

The update also introduces a new railgun-type weapon - [b]Large Railgun[/b]. The new railgun, like the artillery gun, inflicts a lot of damage per single hit, it is relatively slow to aim, and has a significant cost. Unlike the artillery gun, the new weapon shoots very fast projectiles that can reach their targets almost instantly.

The [b]EMP Gun[/b], instead of inflicting damage, drains the energy of its target by a set amount per hit. Its projectiles also immobilize the target unit for a few seconds. EMP guns are very useful against fliers, which can be trapped and destroyed with a few well placed shots.

[h1]Other[/h1]
[list]
[*]New skirmish map ([b]Islands[/b]);
[*]Sandbox changed to include the Marine Factory;
[*]Regular Railgun balance changes (decreased range to 7.5);
[*]Various interface improvements and fixes.
[/list]

notes.title: Update Notes: Large Walker Legs, Propulsion Module Configuration
notes.notes:
[h1]What's new?[/h1]

The update introduces a new propulsion module ([b]Large Walker Leg[/b]), a much improved automatic unit stability model, as well as the ability to control its influence. Furthermore, it adds a few new structural modules; various other minor fixes and improvements are also included.

[h1]Walker Legs[/h1]

This update adds a new walker leg class propulsion module - [b]Large Walker Leg[/b]. It can support greater weight and is more stable than the regular walker leg. Like the regular leg, the larger leg is retractable.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/b3b0c38f586a87a9c3ded25619f9238cd8fa29e6.png[/img]

In addition to the new module, walker leg physics model has been tweaked and improved upon. As of this update, walker units of all types should have better overall handling.

Other walker leg related changes and additions:

[list]
[*]Extend/Retract Legs - extension and retraction of legs and telescopic beams are no longer combined into one command. In order to extend and retract legs use the new [b]Extend/Retract Legs[/b] command (default hotkey: C);
[*]Legs are now auto-extended when the unit wants to move - but only when no wheels, tracks or screws are present and the walker is not currently in water with working water jets.
[*]Leg energy consumption has been changed, so that lighter units consume slightly more energy than they used to.
[/list]

[h1]Stability Control and Advanced Module Configuration[/h1]

The new Stability Control model greatly improves the handling and viability of lighter units. It may also improve the performance of heavier units, but the effect will most likely be not as drastic.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/48896ace27fc3b686bca6303c968a0c66dd9b4c7.gif[/img]

The unit on the left has its stability control disabled. Too much power delivered to its wheels cause it to roll excessively. The unit on the right with the stability control enabled has no trouble moving at normal speed.

[b]Stability Control[/b] influence is set to 100% for all ground propulsion devices by default; it is the recommended setting for most units. However, reducing it may improve speed and acceleration for some light units with non-standard wheel configurations. This setting can be set on a per-wheel basis (accessed via Configure Modules from the Unit Designer).

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/eecbf5d089ec29d8a9495c3166d7f2ed541728ea.png[/img]

The maximum power the wheel can utilize can also be adjusted; the recommended setting here is 100% as well.

[h1]Structural Modules[/h1]

The update adds two new structural modules: [b]Spherical Hull[/b] and [b]Half-Spherical Hull[/b]. Both modules have colorable and reflective versions, and both can be modified.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/4bd55a24b105fa11a37e4b0b5af4d1ed994f2925.png[/img]

[h1]Other[/h1]

Minor fixes and improvements include:
[list]
[*]Air [b]Fans[/b] can now be configured: as before, the fans are engaged only when no wheels, tracks, screws or legs touch the ground by default; though now they can be configured to drive the unit at all times.
[*]Unit and building indicator bar size reduced when the camera is zoomed out;
[*]In-game chat has been improved;
[*]Larger tall units are no longer delayed upon deployment when transported on belts;
[*]Minor campaign balance changes.
[*]Other minor interface fixes and improvements.
[/list]

notes.title: Update Notes: Radar, Reactor, Additional Unit Slots
notes.notes:
[h1]What's New?[/h1]

This latest update brings a new systems module, a facility to convert resources, as well as many gameplay and user interface improvements - including the ability to assign custom unit hotkeys. The player can now also build twice as many units in skirmish and multiplayer modes.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/cd0b841acf2b95a83451d3952f08a05576b756c9.png[/img]

[h1]Radar[/h1]

A new module that increases unit's sight range. Any one unit can be equipped with up to 5 radar devices (one radar per computer). For every radar equipped the unit gains a set increase in sight range.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/45798ab5d398216dbe246748ab2fbbbeee306530.png[/img]

[h1]Reactor[/h1]

A new facility that allows resource conversion (Heavy Pellets to Pellets). Useful in situations where the player ends up with an excess of Heavy Pellets and a deficit of regular Pellets making it impossible to produce units.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/4231730c8f8c084952de9cd6f4d95faee3218ef8.png[/img]

[h1]Hotkeys[/h1]

In addition to an expanded overall hotkey set, the player can now assign custom one-letter unit hotkeys. This feature also works with generic weapon racks - by holding the hotkey button instead of pressing it, the weapon selection window will appear; from there only a single click is required to switch weapons.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/781c4fc7fd8c3acae949ae177aafca5209cf48e5.png[/img]

[h1]More Slots[/h1]

The number of [i]Slots[/i] in skirmish and multiplayer games was increased from from 100 to 200. The number of Slots in the campaign has also gone up significantly.

[h1]Sample Repository[/h1]

The game now also comes with a sample unit repository. It contains several units that demonstrate module usage; they can be useful as an introduction to unit buliding, or a quick way to start playing without the need to design everything from ground up.

[list]
[*]General interface improvements including the map selection menu, repository menu, etc.
[*]Various optimizations and bug fixes.
[/list]

notes.title: Update Notes: Expanded Base Building
notes.notes:
[h1]What's New?[/h1]

With this latest update players can now build additional [b]Build Pads[/b] and [b]Factory Pads[/b] (Field Factories) anywhere on the map. New [b]Build Pads[/b] can be established near any [b]Construction Tower[/b] (a new special building type also introduced with this update).

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/bf0319df9fd35ce0331934870d1b280f82494afe.png[/img]

[h1]New Building Types[/h1]

[list]
[*][b]Field Factory[/b] - just like any other factory this structure is able to construct units. However, while regular Factories cannot get damaged, Field Factories have a limited amount of hit points (350), and thusly can be destroyed;
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/f29980d7d2e71caf0a89ed92d463fa35d9b2102f.png[/img]

[*][b]Construction Tower[/b] - a building which is capable of constructing new build pads, and has greater vision range than most buildings;
[*][b]Barrier[/b] - a relatively cheap way to cordon off and block parts of the map.
[/list]

[h1]New Weapon: Fragmentation Launcher[/h1]

[b]Fragmentation Launcher[/b] is a new projectile weapon. It is the least powerful rocket-based weapon. However, what it lacks in firepower it makes up in splash damage - making it useful against swarming enemy units.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/45e571362dad5999db060553aad42db742b7fcfe.png[/img]

[h1]Balance Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Resource amount per patch increased from 500 to 1000;
[*]Rocket based weapon firepower and hit damage reduced;
[*]Skirmish map bases modified in order to facilitate new build construction.
[/list]

[h1]Other[/h1]

Various minor bug fixes and improvements.

notes.title: Update: Artillery, Extended Zoom Range, Auto-Reorient Behavior
notes.notes:
The update includes:

[h1]Artillery[/h1]

[b]Artillery Gun[/b] is a new powerful, long range weapon. It deals a lot of damage in a single hit and has a very long reach, but is quite slow moving. Its projectiles have a ballistic trajectory and take some time to land. Because of these limitations and the fact that this gun can fire much further than the unit can see, it's recommended to always send supporting units together with the artillery.

Other factors to take into account when designing an artillery unit:
[list]
[*]Recoil - [i]Artillery Gun[/i] has significant recoil. If the unit in question is not stable enough it might be in danger of flipping over. Additionally, any unit movement during a shot will dramatically reduce its accuracy.
[*][i]Artillery Gun[/i] counts as two weapons when installed on the unit, and thus a 5 slot unit can have only one weapon of this type.
[/list]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/d22bac88ee48d4e88d82b44c6f771b35dbb2a671.png[/img]

[h1]New Unit Behavior[/h1]
[b]Auto Re-orient Behavior[/b] (Toggle Icon: [img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/35918194f35a0aa1ad7abd5336dd0c2d87383f00.png[/img]) - units that are equipped with magnets and have this behavior enabled will automatically try to reorient nearby upturned friendly units. If the unit performing the action is busy [i]mining[/i] or [i]moving[/i], it will pause its current task until the target unit is set back upright. This behavior is enabled by default.

[h1]Extended Zoom Range[/h1]

The camera can now zoom out significantly further out (50% increase).

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25738567/e746aa372fe01c3ac6129623207e8b8910d9de46.png[/img]

[h1]Other[/h1]
[list]
[*]Minor interface improvements;
[*]Minor campaign balance changes;
[*]Various bug fixes.
[/list]

notes.title: New Unit Designer is out now!
notes.notes:
The game now features a completely new unit designer. This time, rather than instructing the factory how to build the unit, the player is be able to design the unit by freely snapping modules together. This allows for a much faster and easier creation of complex units.

Check out the preview from last week to get an idea how it works:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4ko0a3x3mdk
Note: You can still use the old "Linear" unit designer if you wish. To switch to the old unit designer: go to Options -> Other -> Fabrication, and click the appropriate designer icon.

[h1]Converting Units For Use With the New Designer[/h1]

To convert units created with the old Linear Unit Designer, please follow these steps:
[list]
[*]Enable the [b]Snap Designer[/b]; (Options -> Other -> Fabrication; enabled by default)
[*]When in game, go to Unit Gallery and Clone the units you wish to convert;
[*]The newly cloned unit will be automatically converted for use with the new Snap Designer;
[/list]
[h1]Other Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*]The maximum number of modules has gone up from 200 to 300. (25 additional modules per auxiliary computer)
[*]Minor campaign tweaks;
[*]Minor bug fixes;
[/list]
